data: This course will build social psychological foundations for the sociality of the self, interpersonal relationships, and group behaviour in Psychology. This will serve three important and interconnected purposes. Firstly, students will learn to think about social psychological research and some of the classic studies in nuanced and complex ways. Secondly, students will learn to critically appraise the work and findings of social psychological concepts reported in public discourse. Finally, students will learn to expand their concepts of the self as social beings with multiple social identities and bring these to bear upon their interpretation of social behaviour. The course will bridge the gap between simplified concepts in standard social psychology textbooks and the rigour, complexity and uncertainty of findings in the primary literature, including, among others, journals and theses.
